## Context / Problem

Ticket e39f-5055-f5af-424a makes the reconciler's inbound link-removal path (G5, apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one) converge by removing exactly the mirrored (target, relation) link. The safety analysis surfaced a PRE-EXISTING blind spot inherited from 2b16's design: managed_refs marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY (reducer/_managed_refs.py — strictly monotonic), so G3 cannot distinguish a brand-new never-pushed local link from a peer-deleted one. G4 (same-pass outbound-ADD suppression) covers that blind spot ONLY when the outbound differ emits the re-ADD; outbound_links.py::_diff_links dedups ADDs direction-agnostically on (vendor_type, target_key) ('intentionally NOT deduped on relation'), so a local link whose vendor type collides with an existing remote link in the other direction (blocks vs inward Blocks) is never pushed AND not G4-protected — an inbound removal record for it can reach G5 and remove a never-pushed local link. This is order-dependently true TODAY (when the never-pushed link is the pair's most-recent, pair-scoped unlink removes it after G5's relation match passes); e39f makes the outcome order-independent but does not add a discriminator.

## Approach

Design pass: persist enough peer-link history (e.g. record (relation, target) as 'peer-confirmed' only after an outbound link ADD is successfully applied or the link is observed in a fetched snapshot) so _inbound_unlink_one can decline removals of never-peer-confirmed links. Must reconcile with managed_refs monotonicity and compaction (SNAPSHOT restore).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a removal record for a managed-but-never-peer-confirmed link is declined and logged.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k declines`
- [x] a removal for a peer-confirmed link still converges.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k converges`
- [x] behavior covered by behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations/_inbound_update_apply_links.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py`
- [x] all four children (S1-S4) are closed and their changes are Verified +1 on Gerrit.
      Proof: `rebar list --parent despotic-floriated-leopard` shows every child `closed`

## Testing

Each child carries its own suite and gate commands; the epic is proven by the union of them:
`make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` green on the final child,
plus the existing `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py`
regression suite staying green throughout.

## Chosen direction (operator-approved 2026-08-12; research comments above are the evidence base)

Follow the pattern both maintained comparisons converge on (GitHub ghas-jira-integration; contrast softrams/bulwark): **retain durable association/provenance and perform explicit managed mutations; never treat an unqualified missing link as deletion evidence.**

Concretely: persist a **full peer-confirmation record** per managed link (Jira linkId, direction, the confirming snapshot revision, confirmed-at time) — not a minimal boolean — because Jira exposes deletion as an explicit event keyed by stable linkId, and the completeness tracking S2 needs is impossible with a boolean. A partial/paginated/failed read is NON-EVIDENCE. Backfill grandfathers existing managed links as confirmed-at-upgrade (marked as such) so the first post-upgrade run does not decline every legitimate removal.

## Decomposition (children)
- S1: define + persist the peer-confirmation record (written on successful outbound link ADD; survives SNAPSHOT compaction; reconciled with managed_refs monotonicity).
- S2: populate confirmations from fetched authoritative snapshots, recording snapshot completeness; partial reads can never confirm nor deny.
- S3: _inbound_unlink_one declines-and-logs removal of never-peer-confirmed links (behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations).
- S4: backfill migration marking existing managed links confirmed-at-upgrade.
